mie:ise-wine.tagline_en: Saperavi by the sacred city: an Ise winery where disabled staff grow, ferment and bottle every drop.
mie:ise-wine.desc_en: Ise Wine was founded in 2021 by the operator of the Job Studio Ise employment-support facility, making it a full agriculture-welfare winery: people with disabilities work every stage from vineyard to cellar. Vines of Saperavi and Sauvignon Blanc are farmed naturally, without herbicides or chemical fertilizer, with crushed pearl-oyster shell feeding the soil — an Ise touch. The work won the 2024 Japan Noufuku Award, and in 2025 the first trio of wines — red Shizuku, white Rin and rosé Miyabi — began pouring at Ise city hotels.
features_en: Agriculture-welfare winery run with Job Studio Ise
2024 Japan Noufuku Award winner
Natural farming with pearl-shell soil amendments

伊勢雫.specs_en: Red — 100% Saperavi, one year in French oak

伊勢雅.specs_en: Rosé — 100% Saperavi, the first rosé made and aged entirely in Ise

kanagawa:kentoku-winery.tagline_en: Sagamihara's only winery, born when a recycling company planted vines to keep its veteran workers employed.
kanagawa:kentoku-winery.desc_en: Kentoku Winery has an unusual origin: recycling firm Omori Sangyo founded a farming subsidiary in 2014 to re-employ its older workers, and the vineyard they planted grew into Sagamihara's only winery. Certified under the city's wine special-zone program, the estate obtained its own license in January 2023 after years of contract winemaking. Everything is estate fruit, released as single-variety 'Sagamihara Wine' from an ambitious range of plantings — Chardonnay, Albariño and Petit Manseng through Cabernet Sauvignon and Muscat Bailey A. Wines are sold online and through local stockists.
features_en: Sagamihara's only winery, self-producing since January 2023
Founded to re-employ a recycling company's senior workers
Single-variety wines from estate-grown fruit only

yamaguchi:domaine-pinot-livre.tagline_en: A members-only island domaine in the Seto Inland Sea, two vignerons and a single grape: Yama Sauvignon.
yamaguchi:domaine-pinot-livre.desc_en: On Suo-Oshima island, Domaine Pinot Livre has pursued one ideal since 2018: to be vignerons for life. Two grower-winemakers farm only their own vineyards of Yama Sauvignon — a Japanese cross of wild mountain grape and Cabernet Sauvignon — and handle every step themselves, brewing minimally and without fixed recipes. Distribution is equally uncompromising: the winery operates as a closed, members-club estate whose annual allocation was fully subscribed for 2025, though limited releases appear in its web shop and the on-site shop opens by advance reservation.
features_en: All estate fruit, tended by just two vigneron-owners
Closed members-club distribution model
Minimal, recipe-free winemaking

osaka:toyono-takayama-winery.tagline_en: Abandoned rice terraces in Osaka's northern hills, replanted with vines at 500 meters.
osaka:toyono-takayama-winery.desc_en: Toyono Takayama Winery grew out of a satoyama-revival project: its parent, founded in 2020, cleared derelict rice terraces in the hills of Toyono and replanted them with vines. Licensed in March 2024, the estate uses the cool climate at roughly 500 meters and clear spring water to grow and ferment everything on site, releasing its first 2025 vintage from Muscat Bailey A, Sauvignon Blanc, Delaware and Yama Sauvignon. Under the local wine special-zone program, the wines pour at the Auberge Yamagami and at events around the town.
features_en: Reclaimed terraced rice fields turned vineyard
About 500 m elevation with mountain spring water
First vintage 2025; served at the local auberge

マスカット・ベーリーA ペティアン.specs_en: Sparkling — gently fizzy Muscat Bailey A

hokkaido:hamada-vineyard.tagline_en: A second-career couple on a Mikasa hillside, growing Bacchus and Pinot Noir one row at a time.
hokkaido:hamada-vineyard.desc_en: Hamada Vineyard sits on the Tappu hills of Mikasa, farmed by a husband-and-wife team who left earlier careers — one a University of Tokyo medical graduate — and retrained for about a year at Mikasa's Yamazaki Winery before planting their own vines. The first harvest came in autumn 2018 and the first release a year later. Since 2021 the wines, led by Bacchus and Pinot Noir, have been made at a domaine the couple co-founded with a neighboring vineyard.
features_en: Family-run vineyard on Mikasa's Tappu hills
Trained at Yamazaki Winery before first planting
First harvest 2018; wines made at a co-founded domaine since 2021

yamanashi:vineyard-kikushima.tagline_en: Wild-yeast Katsunuma wines from borrowed vineyards — a boutique estate keeping aging farmland alive.
yamanashi:vineyard-kikushima.desc_en: Vineyards Kikushima began with contract-made Koshu and Merlot in 2016, then built its own boutique winery in Katsunuma in 2020. The house works to a philosophy it calls gentle winemaking: no chemical pesticides or insecticides in the vineyard, wild-yeast fermentation in the cellar. Just as important is where the grapes come from — plots borrowed from aging farmers, keeping Katsunuma's vineyard landscape in production. Sales are limited to the first Saturdays of April and November and by appointment, which only adds to the small-estate character.
features_en: No chemical pesticides; wild-yeast fermentation
Farms plots borrowed from aging growers
About 90 ares across Koshu, Merlot, Pinot Noir and more

Nomujan ベーリーA Rouge.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A with a little Cabernet Sauvignon (2022)

tottori:kurayoshi-winery.tagline_en: Wine from a preserved merchant townhouse in Kurayoshi, with vines on Tottori's central dunes.
tottori:kurayoshi-winery.desc_en: Kurayoshi Winery took shape after three neighboring municipalities won a joint wine special-zone designation in 2017; the company followed in July 2018, setting its cellar inside a machiya townhouse in Kurayoshi's nationally designated historic preservation district. Grapes — Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and the table grape Pione — grow on the sandy soils of Tottori's central dune fields, and everything from farming to fermentation stays in-house under the Hakushu label. A café, shop and tasting corner welcome visitors, with an online shop for the rest of the country.
features_en: Cellar in a nationally preserved merchant townhouse
Vineyards on Tottori's central sand-dune soils
Everything grown and fermented in-house

miyagi:minamisanriku-winery.tagline_en: A winery with the sea in its windows — Minamisanriku's first, built by two regional-revitalization volunteers.
miyagi:minamisanriku-winery.desc_en: Minamisanriku Winery grew from a wine project started in 2017 by two members of the town's regional revitalization corps, incorporated in 2019, and opened in October 2020 with a shop and kitchen looking out over the water. The town's first winery, it ferments grapes grown across Yamagata Prefecture — from Tendo, Tsuruoka, Sagae and beyond — into a food-minded range that runs from Koshu sur lie to Delaware sparkling. The shop opens most afternoons, with winery experiences on offer.
features_en: Minamisanriku's first winery, opened 2020
Founded by two regional-revitalization corps members
Sea-view shop and kitchen at the cellar

iwate:ohsama-sato-vineyard.tagline_en: An engineer turned grower in the Hanamaki hills, running his vineyard on data and aiming wine at washoku.
iwate:ohsama-sato-vineyard.desc_en: Ohsama Sato Vineyard farms 70 ares in the mountains of Odashima, Hanamaki, where a former medical-device engineer changed careers in 2016, planted vines in 2017 and opened his winery in 2021 — the second under the Hanamaki craft wine and cider special zone. The vineyard is run like the lab he came from: thorough data analysis guides the growing, vine by vine and cluster by cluster. All fruit is estate-grown Merlot and Zweigeltrebe, and the target is clear — dry wines that sit comfortably beside Japanese food. Visits are possible with advance consultation.
features_en: Hanamaki special-zone winery no. 2 (2021)
Data-driven 'smart' viticulture by a former engineer
100% estate fruit, aimed at dry, washoku-friendly wine

hiroshima:hokkoh-winery.tagline_en: Gravity does the work at this Chugoku-mountain cellar, built for the wild-blooded Yamasauvignon grape.
hiroshima:hokkoh-winery.desc_en: Hokkoh Winery began harvesting Yamasauvignon in 2007, and when the crop passed three tons, built a new cellar in 2018 beside the Karashiro-kan hall in Kitahiroshima. The site, on the cool skirts of the Chugoku mountains with wide day-night temperature swings, suits Yamasauvignon and Cabernet Sauvignon, and the winery itself is laid out on a gravity-flow plan — no pumps push the wine. A cider from local apples rounds out the range. Wines are sold online and through regional retailers, with occasional tasting events.
features_en: Cool, high-contrast climate at the foot of the Chugoku range
Gravity-flow winery, no pumping
Also makes cider from Kitahiroshima apples

山紫野.specs_en: Red — Yamasauvignon and Cabernet Sauvignon; Reserve 2020

nagasaki:obama-onsen-winery.tagline_en: An Italian chef came home to Unzen's hot-spring coast — and planted 1,900 vines on abandoned fields.
nagasaki:obama-onsen-winery.desc_en: Obama Onsen Winery is the project of chef Takahiro Kawashima, who returned from Nagano to his home region and began planting abandoned farmland in Unzen in April 2020. By September 2021 he had opened a winery and Italian restaurant, the Obama Wine Shokudo, in the hot-spring town itself. Across six reclaimed plots grow about 1,900 vines of eight varieties, from Albariño and Chardonnay to Campbell Early, all fermented in-house. The restaurant runs on advance reservations, pairing the wines with the chef's cooking.
features_en: Founded by a U-turn Italian chef in 2020–21
1,900 vines of eight varieties on six reclaimed plots
Winery-restaurant in the Obama hot-spring town

kanagawa:kuratei-winery-domaine-yamada.tagline_en: A 130-year-old kura turned winery on a Kawasaki hillside, pouring Pinot Noir and Chardonnay by the glass under local zoning.
kanagawa:kuratei-winery-domaine-yamada.desc_en: Carna Est, an agricultural producer corporation, began growing grapes in 2014 and opened Kuratei Winery Domaine Yamada in 2020, on a hillside in Kawasaki's Asao Ward, about 25 kilometers from central Tokyo. The winery occupies a renovated 130-year-old kura and focuses on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It also houses a wine school, a wine bar and shop, and the farm restaurant Lilly's. by promety. Under Kawasaki's House Wine Special Zone system, the winery may serve wine by the glass on-site only — bottle sales are not permitted.
features_en: Grape growing began in 2014; the winery opened in 2020 in a renovated 130-year-old kura
Under Kawasaki's House Wine Special Zone system, only by-the-glass pours are allowed — no bottle sales
Houses a wine school, wine bar, and the farm restaurant Lilly's. by promety

miyagi:fattoria-al-fiore.tagline_en: A former elementary school gymnasium in Kawasaki-machi, Miyagi, now ferments natural, no-additive wines from Delaware, Muscat Bailey A and other grapes.
miyagi:fattoria-al-fiore.desc_en: Fattoria al Fiore opened in 2018 in a former elementary school gymnasium in Kawasaki-machi, Miyagi, run by Meglot Co., Ltd. The winery makes natural, no-additive wines — red, white and orange — from a wide range of grapes including Delaware and Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red), set amid the satoyama countryside. Its guiding philosophy, in the winery's own words: 'Grapes are alive. Our wine is alive, too... we treat our grapes and wine gently, the same way we treat our friends.'
features_en: Housed in a former elementary school gymnasium in Kawasaki-machi
Natural, no-additive winemaking
Set in the satoyama countryside of Kawasaki-machi, Miyagi

Fattoria AL FIORE.specs_en: Red, white and orange — a natural series using diverse grapes such as Delaware and Muscat Bailey A

ibaraki:tsukuba-vineyard-kurihara.tagline_en: Petit Manseng planted on fallow land in 2014 grew into a 2.3-hectare estate, now home to 13 grape varieties at Tsukuba's sixth-industrialization winery.
ibaraki:tsukuba-vineyard-kurihara.desc_en: Led by Manabu Takahashi, the project began in 2014 with Petit Manseng vines planted on roughly 1,000 square meters of fallow farmland. The vineyard grew to about 2.3 hectares, and in December 2019 it received Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries certification as a sixth-industrialization project. In August 2020 it obtained a manufacturing license under the Tsukuba Wine & Fruit Liquor Special Zone and opened its own brewing facility, Kurihara Winery — until then, wine had been made under contract by a sake brewer in Chikusei. A separate, unrelated company also operates as 'Tsukuba Winery' in the same city.
features_en: Fallow land planted with Petit Manseng in 2014 has grown into a 2.3-hectare estate growing 13 grape varieties
Certified as a sixth-industrialization project by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries in December 2019; licensed under the Tsukuba Wine & Fruit Liquor Special Zone in August 2020
Awarded three stars in the Japan Winery Award, per the winery's official blog

ehime:blue-wax-winery.tagline_en: Opening in December 2025 on Matsuyama's Okaido arcade, Blue Wax Winery is Chugoku-Shikoku's first urban winery, launched with national grant support.
ehime:blue-wax-winery.desc_en: Blue Wax Winery opened on December 2, 2025 on Okaido, Matsuyama's central shopping street, as the first urban winery in the Chugoku-Shikoku region. The roughly 430-square-meter, two-story building houses brewing equipment, a shop and bar cafe on the first floor, with a restaurant on the second. It produces original wines from grapes harvested in Takayama Village, Nagano Prefecture, and Kumakogen, Ehime Prefecture, alongside a curated selection of wines from across Japan. The project was launched with funding from the national and Matsuyama municipal governments after being selected for the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' 'Local 10,000 Project.'
features_en: Opened December 2, 2025 as the first urban winery in the Chugoku-Shikoku region
Brewing equipment, shop and bar cafe on the first floor; restaurant on the second
Selected for the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' 'Local 10,000 Project,' with national and Matsuyama municipal funding

hokkaido:nitori-winery.tagline_en: Nitori Fruit Orchard in Yoichi began growing Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in 2022, opening its own winery in 2025 after years of contract brewing.
hokkaido:nitori-winery.desc_en: Nitori Fruit Orchard, a pick-your-own tourist orchard in Yoichi, began growing wine grapes such as Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in 2022. Until then, its grapes went to contract brewing at other wineries — producing about 370 bottles of white wine in 2023, then roughly 1,800 bottles of white, red and rose in 2024. In April 2025 the orchard obtained a fruit-wine manufacturing license, and from that autumn began brewing under its own label as Nitori Winery, targeting about 3,000 bottles in its first year.
features_en: A pick-your-own tourist orchard that began growing Pinot Noir and Chardonnay for wine in 2022
Obtained a fruit-wine manufacturing license in April 2025 and began brewing under its own label that autumn
Before licensing, grapes went to contract brewing — about 1,800 bottles of white, red and rose in 2024

yamanashi:domaine-mie-ikeno.tagline_en: At 750 meters on Yatsugatake's southern slopes, Domaine Mie Ikeno's 'sky vineyard' makes Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Merlot via pump-free gravity flow.
yamanashi:domaine-mie-ikeno.desc_en: Domaine Mie Ikeno began growing grapes in spring 2007 on hillsides along the southern foot of Mt. Yatsugatake, and the winery itself was born when its brewery was built in autumn 2011. At 750 meters elevation, the vineyard looks out over the Southern Alps and Mt. Fuji, and is known as the 'sky vineyard' for how clouds wrap the fields after rain. Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Merlot are grown here and vinified using a pump-free gravity-flow system that keeps the grapes from being jostled. The brewery building itself was architect-designed.
features_en: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Merlot grown at 750 meters on Yatsugatake's southern slopes, overlooking the Southern Alps and Mt. Fuji
A pump-free gravity-flow system minimizes stress on the grapes during vinification
An architect-designed brewery building

hokkaido:nakazawa-vineyard.tagline_en: Kazuyuki and Yukiko Nakazawa broke ground on a 2.7-hectare vineyard in Iwamizawa in 2002, whole-cluster pressed and wild-yeast fermented into Kurisawa Blanc.
hokkaido:nakazawa-vineyard.desc_en: In 2002, Kazuyuki and Yukiko Nakazawa took up farming and cleared roughly 2.7 hectares of dedicated wine-grape vineyard in Iwamizawa's former Kurisawa-cho. From 2002 to 2012 their grapes were vinified under contract at Coco Farm, and from 2013 at 10R Winery; since 2017 they have brewed at Kurisawa Wines, a brewery they co-founded. Their method presses grapes whole-cluster and ferments with wild yeast.
features_en: Kazuyuki and Yukiko Nakazawa took up farming in 2002 and cleared a dedicated wine-grape vineyard in Iwamizawa's Kurisawa-cho
Contract-brewed at Coco Farm, then 10R Winery, before moving to their own co-founded Kurisawa Wines brewery in 2017
Flagship Kurisawa Blanc is whole-cluster pressed and wild-yeast fermented

クリサワブラン.specs_en: White — blend of Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris, Kerner, Sylvaner and others

aichi:winar-nagoya.tagline_en: Launched March 16, 2025 in Nagoya's Endoji shopping district, WINAR is an urban winery pouring Albariño and Syrah from its own Midori Ward vineyard.
aichi:winar-nagoya.desc_en: Nagoya Winery WINAR began full operations on March 16, 2025 in the Endoji shopping district of Nagoya's Nishi Ward, as an urban winery. It is run by Verazon Co., Ltd., headquartered in Tokoname, Aichi Prefecture — the same company behind Tokoname Winery, a separate facility. Its debut vintage was made from Albariño (white) and Syrah (red) grown in the company's own vineyard in Nagoya's Midori Ward.
features_en: An urban winery in central Nagoya, built around the 'POST CULTIVATE' concept of rethinking cultivating, growing and eating to build community
Debut vintage released March 16, 2025, from Albariño and Syrah grown since 2022 in the company's own Midori Ward vineyard
Run by Verazon Co., Ltd., which also operates the separate Tokoname Winery in Tokoname, Aichi

hokkaido:miyamoto-vineyard.tagline_en: Since 2012, Miyamoto Vineyard has farmed a steep 3-hectare plot in Mikasa's Tappu district, growing Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris.
hokkaido:miyamoto-vineyard.desc_en: In spring 2012, Ryohei Miyamoto cleared a dedicated wine-grape vineyard of about 3 hectares and 8,000 vines in the Tappu district of Mikasa, Hokkaido. After training at Obuse Winery, in New Zealand, and with a winemaker in Burgundy, he planted Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris. Through the 2020 vintage, grapes were vinified under contract at the neighboring Takizawa Winery, on a steep hillside plot.
features_en: Ryohei Miyamoto cleared a dedicated wine-grape vineyard in Mikasa's Tappu district in 2012
Trained at Obuse Winery, in New Zealand and in Burgundy before focusing on Pinot Noir
A roughly 3-hectare, 8,000-vine steep hillside plot next to Takizawa Winery, contract-brewed there through the 2020 vintage

kochi:mishima-farm-winery.tagline_en: Rooted in a grape farm founded in 1960, Mishima Farm Winery earned Kochi Prefecture's first fruit-wine license in 2017 and began vinifying in 2018.
kochi:mishima-farm-winery.desc_en: Mishima Farm Winery grew out of a grape farm founded in 1960, led by Toshio Yamanaka. In December 2016, Tosa-cho was designated a 'wine special zone,' and in June 2017 the farm obtained Kochi Prefecture's first fruit-wine manufacturing license, beginning wine production in 2018. It uses chemical-pesticide-free table grapes alongside dedicated wine varieties such as Merlot and Pinot Noir.
features_en: Obtained Kochi Prefecture's first fruit-wine manufacturing license in June 2017
Committed to chemical-pesticide-free table grape growing
Makes wine from both table grapes and dedicated wine varieties such as Merlot and Pinot Noir

yamanashi:98wines.tagline_en: Deep in the mountains above Shioyama, 98WINEs crafts Koshu and Muscat Bailey A into three tiers — Sou, Nogi and Koku — with sulfite-free brewing.
yamanashi:98wines.desc_en: 98WINEs opened in 2017 in Shioyama, Koshu City, envisioned as a place exploring 'the power that wine holds' and connecting people through it. The winery focuses solely on Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) and Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red), achieving sulfite-free vinification since 2020 through precise cellar management and gravity-flow methods that minimize stress on the grapes. Its site in Fukuori, a former community-hall lot with views of Mt. Fuji, comprises three buildings: an 'iron wing' for brewing, a 'stone wing' for storage, and a 'wood wing' for gathering.
features_en: A mountain winery above Shioyama focused solely on Koshu and Muscat Bailey A
Sulfite-free vinification since 2020 through precise cellar management, with gravity-flow methods to minimize stress on the grapes
Three buildings — brewing ('iron wing'), storage ('stone wing') and gathering ('wood wing') — on a former community-hall site in Fukuori, with Mt. Fuji views

okayama:kibi-valley.tagline_en: Kibi Chuo's only winery ferments 100% town-grown grapes, chilling hand-picked Pione for its whites and oak-aging Muscat Bailey A, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon reds.
okayama:kibi-valley.desc_en: Completed in December 2020, kibi VALLEY is the only winery in Kibi Chuo, vinifying grapes grown entirely within the town. For its white wine, hand-picked Pione grapes are chilled and aged in cold storage before pressing; its reds — Muscat Bailey A, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon — are aged in oak barrels. The winery holds certification under the 'Dereh Umee Wine Special Zone,' named for the local dialect phrase for 'really delicious.'
features_en: The only winery in Kibi Chuo, vinifying 100% town-grown grapes
Certified under the 'Dereh Umee Wine Special Zone'
Whites from hand-picked Pione, chilled and aged before pressing; reds aged in oak barrels

miyagi:chateau-kiri-kurikoma.tagline_en: Kirishiro, an agriculture-and-welfare company in Kurikoma, grows its own Muscat Bailey A and Merlot for unfiltered, sulfite-free wines, including the 39WINE collaboration.
miyagi:chateau-kiri-kurikoma.desc_en: Chateau Kiri Kurikoma Kogen Winery is run by Kirishiro Co., Ltd., a company active in agriculture, school lunches and welfare services. It sorts its own estate-grown Kurikoma grapes — Muscat Bailey A, Merlot and others — and vinifies them at a brewery adjoining the vineyard, using methods that avoid added sulfites and filtration. The winery also produces 39WINE, made in collaboration with a support facility for people with disabilities.
features_en: Partners with a local employment-support facility for people with disabilities on grape growing and label affixing, as an agriculture-welfare collaboration
Estate-grown Kurikoma grapes vinified at a brewery adjoining the vineyard
No added sulfites, unfiltered winemaking

Merlot 2022 Kurikoma Wine.specs_en: Red — estate-grown Merlot (Kurikoma-grown), no added sulfites

iwate:kanda-budo-wine.tagline_en: Founded in 2015 by a beverage maker dating to 1905, Kanda Vineyard grows Albariño on salt-sprayed Sanriku hillsides to pair with local seafood.
iwate:kanda-budo-wine.desc_en: Kanda Vineyard was launched in 2015 by a beverage company founded in 1905, growing Albariño on 2.5 hectares of its own vineyard along the Sanriku coast. The concept behind its label, THE RIAS WINE, is wine that pairs with Sanriku's abundant seafood. Grapes grown in salt-tinged soil exposed to sea breezes yield wines with a distinct minerality.
features_en: A winery on the Sanriku coast
Built around the concept of pairing wine with Sanriku's seafood
2.5 hectares of estate vineyard
Rooted in a beverage company founded in 1905

hokkaido:libera-wine-terrace.tagline_en: Founded in 2024, this urban Sapporo winery uses Kimura-method natural, chemical-free farming and AI management, returning 80% of sales to disability employment.
hokkaido:libera-wine-terrace.desc_en: LIBERA WINE TERRACE, founded in 2024 and known as 'Sapporo Botanical Garden Brewing — Hokkaido Natural Cultivation Agricultural School,' is an urban winery that grows its grapes without pesticides, chemical fertilizers or herbicides, using the Kimura method of natural farming. AI-assisted cultivation and brewing management help create a safe working environment for people with disabilities, as part of a social-enterprise model that returns 80% of sales to disability employment and environmental improvement.
features_en: An urban brewery known as 'Sapporo Botanical Garden Brewing'
A social enterprise: 80% of sales support disability employment and environmental improvement
Kimura-method natural, chemical-free farming with AI-assisted management

kanagawa:yokohama-kajitsu-jozo.tagline_en: A Yokohama welfare foundation's new winery turns overlooked 'hamanashi' pears and local grapes into petillant, blanc and clairet-style wines from autumn 2026.
kanagawa:yokohama-kajitsu-jozo.desc_en: Nakagawa Tokusei-kai, a social welfare corporation, obtained a liquor manufacturing license on July 2, 2026 and launched this Yokohama-born winery. It was created to circulate local resources by using 'hamanashi' — off-grade Yokohama-grown pears that had gone underused — along with Yokohama-grown grapes. Sales are set to begin in early autumn.
features_en: A new Yokohama winery run by a social welfare corporation, licensed on July 2, 2026
Uses off-grade 'hamanashi' Yokohama pears and Yokohama-grown grapes to circulate local resources

chiba:funabashi-coq-winery.tagline_en: The owner of wine-and-meat bistro COQ DINER opened Chiba's first walk-to-station urban winery in 2021, hand-crafting unfiltered wines bottle by bottle.
chiba:funabashi-coq-winery.desc_en: Funabashi COQ Winery was opened by Kokubo, owner of the wine-and-meat restaurant COQ DINER, as Chiba Prefecture's third winery. He applied for a manufacturing license starting in February 2021 and obtained a fruit-wine license that September. It is Chiba's first urban winery within walking distance of a station, making craft wines almost entirely by hand, without filtration.
features_en: Chiba's first urban winery within walking distance of a station
Craft wines made almost entirely by hand, without filtration
Wines sold at the owner's own restaurant, Wine and Meat COQ DINER

ファン ブラック・クイーン＆サンジョヴェーゼ.specs_en: Red, field blend — Black Queen and Sangiovese

iwate:social-farm-winery.tagline_en: Born from Tono Magokoro Net's tsunami-recovery mission, this NPO winery employs disaster survivors and people with disabilities, growing 11 grape varieties on two farms.
iwate:social-farm-winery.desc_en: Social Farm & Winery was founded by the NPO Tono Magokoro Net to revitalize communities affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake and create jobs for disaster survivors and people with disabilities. Grape planting began in 2014, with cultivation of grapes and herbs carried out through the employment of people with disabilities, run as a social-enterprise model for regional revitalization. Eleven varieties of wine grapes are grown across two of the NPO's own farms — in the Ayaori-cho Samukaze district of Tono and in Kasshi-cho, Kamaishi.
features_en: Run by the NPO Tono Magokoro Net
A post-disaster recovery winery from the Great East Japan Earthquake
A social enterprise employing disaster survivors and people with disabilities
Offered as a furusato nozei (hometown tax donation) reward

yamanashi:komaki-vineyard.tagline_en: Sommelier Yasunobu Komaki opened Domaine Enchante in 2025, a stay-in agritourism winery with views of Yatsugatake, Kai-Komagatake and Mt. Fuji.
yamanashi:komaki-vineyard.desc_en: Komaki Vineyard is led by Yasunobu Komaki, a longtime sommelier, and operates as a stay-in winery. In 2025 he opened his own brewery, Domaine Enchante, amid sweeping views of Yatsugatake, Kai-Komagatake and Mt. Fuji, offering an integrated agritourism experience spanning grape growing, winemaking, wine service and lodging.
features_en: Stay-in agritourism with views of Yatsugatake, Kai-Komagatake and Mt. Fuji
Serious winemaking led by a sommelier-qualified owner
A 2025-opened complex with lodging, a cafe and wine tours

fukushima:kawauchi-wine.tagline_en: Villagers and volunteers cleared wasteland at 750 meters in Kawauchi to plant vines in 2015, releasing Village and Riberu wines from a 2021 winery.
fukushima:kawauchi-wine.desc_en: Kawauchi Winery sits in Kawauchi Village, at about 750 meters in the central Abukuma Highlands. Grape growing began in 2015, and the brewing facility was completed in 2021. The winery makes two series: 'Village,' from village-grown grapes, and 'Riberu,' from purchased grapes including fruit from Yoichi, Hokkaido. Its debut vintage was released in March 2022.
features_en: Villagers and volunteers cleared wasteland to establish the vineyard
Two series: 'Village,' from village-grown grapes, and 'Riberu,' from purchased grapes
Winner at the Sakura Award 2026 and Japan Winery Award 2026

iwate:three-peaks.tagline_en: A family winery in seaside Ofunato began with apple cider in 2013 and grew into crisp, mineral-driven dry wines from Chardonnay and Albariño.
iwate:three-peaks.desc_en: Three Peaks is a family-run winery in Ofunato, a coastal city ringed by mountains and sea on the Sanriku coast. It began in 2013 making apple juice and cider, and has since expanded into growing grapes and making wine, producing crisp, mineral-driven dry wines.
features_en: Located on the Sanriku coast in Ofunato
Expanded from apple cider into grape wine
A small, family-run winery

hokkaido:naritaya-winery.tagline_en: Founded in 2020, this soba-and-wine complex in Niki's Asahidai vineyards pairs stone-ground Hokkaido buckwheat noodles with elegant Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Pinot Blanc whites.
hokkaido:naritaya-winery.desc_en: naritaya, founded in 2020, is a soba-and-winery complex surrounded by vineyards in Asahidai, Niki. It grows Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Pinot Blanc, crafting elegant white wines meant to express Asahidai's clear air and terroir. The winery also offers hand-pulled soba made from stone-ground Hokkaido buckwheat flour, paired with its local wines.
features_en: A pairing experience combining hand-pulled soba with local wine
Focused on expressing Asahidai's terroir
An elegant white-wine style

Asahidai 245 Blanc.specs_en: White — Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Pinot Blanc

kumamoto:takahama-wine.tagline_en: Made from Takahama grapes grown locally since around 1879, this rare Amakusa wine sells out on preorder every year, contract-brewed in Yamanashi since 2017.
kumamoto:takahama-wine.desc_en: Takahama Wine uses Takahama grapes — a variety close to Koshu — that have been grown in the area since around 1879. Trial production began in 2015 with the cooperation of Yamato Shuzo in Yamanashi Prefecture, and in 2017 the Takahama Grape Association began full production as its own venture, with brewing still contracted to Yamato Shuzo. Output is limited, and the wine sells out on preorder every year.
features_en: Uses the local specialty Takahama grape, grown since around 1879
Contract-brewed at Yamato Shuzo in Yamanashi since 2017, when full production began
A rare wine, limited in production and sold out on preorder every year

天草高濱甲州ワイン.specs_en: White — contract-brewed at Yamato Shuzo, Yamanashi; Takahama grape (a Koshu-related variety)

yamanashi:cantina-hiro.tagline_en: Winemaker Taiki Hirose trained at Chateau Sakaori and abroad before opening this hilltop winery in 2018, crafting Koshu and Italian varieties without added sugar or acid.
yamanashi:cantina-hiro.desc_en: Cantina Hiro is a small hilltop winery whose wines, in its own words, 'conceal timeless treasures.' Winemaker Taiki Hirose trained at Chateau Sakaori before honing his craft in New Zealand and Australia for about three years, opening the winery in 2018. He took over a grape farm with more than 70 years of history and specializes in Italian varieties alongside Koshu, adding no sugar or acid so as to capture the grapes' natural potential, with an emphasis on fruit character and aroma. The wines are used at Raffles Hotel Singapore, made entirely from estate-grown fruit.
features_en: Winemaker Taiki Hirose trained at Chateau Sakaori, then in New Zealand and Australia for about three years, before opening in 2018
Took over a 70-plus-year-old grape farm and specializes in Italian varieties, adding no sugar or acid
Used at Raffles Hotel Singapore; 100% estate-grown fruit

Felicissimo.specs_en: White, rose, red, orange and sparkling — Italian for 'the happiest'; Koshu, Chardonnay, Muscat Bailey A and Kyoho, including an orange wine (Koshu maceration)

HACCA Anima.specs_en: Red — an Italian-variety series; Nebbiolo and Lambrusco blend

Legame.specs_en: Sparkling and rose — Italian for 'connection, bond'; includes a Koshu Metodo Classico and a Kyoho sparkling

yamanashi:ushioku-daiichi.tagline_en: Operating since 1952, Shioyama's grape farmers pool unsold and off-grade fruit into about 7,000 rare bottles a year, sold almost nowhere but on-site.
yamanashi:ushioku-daiichi.desc_en: Ushioku Daiichi Winery, operating since 1952, is a tiny, farmer-run brewery in Shioyama for the growers' own consumption. Local grape farmers bring in fruit that can't be sold as table grapes, or surplus fruit, to make wine — producing an extremely limited roughly 2,000 bottles of 720ml and 5,000 of 1.8-liter bottles a year. With almost no market distribution, it is known as a wine that can only be bought on-site.
features_en: A farmers'-cooperative micro-winery producing about 7,000 bottles a year
Almost no market distribution — sold only on-site
A locally rooted operation that even sells in traditional 1.8-liter bottles

yamanashi:cave-an.tagline_en: Winemaker Masako Anzo, formerly of Marufuji Budoshu, founded Cave an in 2022, farming six mountain plots in Manriki with Koshu, Petit Manseng, Albariño and Tannat.
yamanashi:cave-an.desc_en: Cave an was founded in 2022 by Masako Anzo, a winemaker formerly responsible for viticulture and winemaking at Marufuji Budoshu. She opened six plots totaling about a hectare in the mountains of Manriki, Yamanashi City, at roughly 400 meters elevation, growing a range of varieties including Koshu, Petit Manseng, Albariño and Tannat. Her aim is balance and elegance suited to Japanese cuisine.
features_en: Founded in 2022 by winemaker Masako Anzo, formerly of Marufuji Budoshu
Six plots totaling about a hectare in Manriki at roughly 400 meters, growing many varieties
Actively introduces European varieties such as Petit Manseng and Albariño

À Table（ア・ターブル）.specs_en: White — an everyday style suited to the table; Koshu and others

万力ブラン.specs_en: White — Koshu grown in the Manriki district

iwate:koto-wine-morioka.tagline_en: Named for four Morioka districts — Kurokawa, Otobe, Teshiromori and Ogao — KOTO Wine turns disused apple orchards and pastures into grapes with disability support.
iwate:koto-wine-morioka.desc_en: Founded in 2021, KOTO Wine Morioka takes its name from the initials of four districts in southeastern Morioka — Kurokawa, Otobe, Teshiromori and Ogao. Born from a local business network aiming to contribute to the community, it connects agriculture and welfare, working with people with disabilities to make wine, and grows grapes on disused apple orchards and pastureland.
features_en: A young winery founded in 2021
A model connecting agriculture and welfare
Provides employment support for people with disabilities

yamanashi:domaine-des-tengeijis.tagline_en: CouCou-Lapin's Domaine des Tengeijis, founded in 2017 under Yumiko Tengeiji, blends organic tradition with modern science to grow Muscat Bailey A sustainably.
yamanashi:domaine-des-tengeijis.desc_en: Domaine des Tengeijis is run by CouCou-Lapin, an agricultural producer corporation, which established the winery in 2017. It practices a 'sustainable farming' approach that combines traditional organic methods with the latest scientific knowledge, growing Muscat Bailey A and other grapes to make wine.
features_en: Practices 'sustainable farming,' combining traditional organic methods with the latest science
Hosts direct sales and workshops at its cellar door
Grows Muscat Bailey A and other grapes under representative Yumiko Tengeiji

aomori:sawauchi-jozo.tagline_en: Chef Akihiro Sawauchi has brewed 'Hachinohe Wine' from Nango-grown grapes since November 2017, alongside cider from apples grown across southern Aomori.
aomori:sawauchi-jozo.desc_en: Sawauchi Jozo began brewing on November 21, 2017, run by Akihiro Sawauchi, chef of an Italian restaurant. It makes 'Hachinohe Wine' from grapes grown in Hachinohe's Nango district, a broader 'Nihon Wine' from grapes grown in Nanbu-cho and Takahata, Yamagata Prefecture, and cider from apples grown across southern Aomori.
features_en: Run by Akihiro Sawauchi, an Italian restaurant chef, at his own brewery
Makes 'Hachinohe Wine' from grapes grown in Hachinohe's Nango district
Also produces cider from apples grown across southern Aomori

yamanashi:domaine-passerelle.tagline_en: At the foot of Yatsugatake, Domaine Passerelle grows JAS-certified organic vines under a 'clean natural,' regenerative farming philosophy.
yamanashi:domaine-passerelle.desc_en: Domaine Passerelle is run by Yatsugatake Organic Vineyard Co., which incorporated in 2020 and brought its winery on line in 2022 in Oizumi, Hokuto. The estate holds JAS organic certification and follows natural-farming methods under a 'Clean Natural' policy centered on regenerative agriculture. Winemaking and viticulture are led by Yuichiro Takahashi. Chardonnay leads a diverse planting that also includes Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Gris, Chenin Blanc, Petit Manseng, Albariño and Gewürztraminer. The winery is not currently open to visitors while it builds out its operations, and its wines are sold only through partner retailers rather than online or direct sales.
features_en: JAS-certified organic and natural farming built around regenerative agriculture
Participant in the '4 per 1000' soil-carbon initiative
Chardonnay, Merlot and Cabernet Franc lead a planting of mostly European varieties

hokkaido:kussharo-caldera-winery.tagline_en: Overlooking Lake Kussharo, this Teshikaga-run winery turned its first vintage of the cold-hardy Yamasachi grape into natural wine in 2024.
hokkaido:kussharo-caldera-winery.desc_en: Kussharo Caldera Winery opened in August 2024 on a site overlooking Lake Kussharo in Teshikaga, run by Teshikaga Farm Co. as a town-designated management project. It makes natural wine from Yamasachi, a cold-hardy grape grown in Teshikaga, with initial annual production of around 2,000 liters. Visitors can taste the wine at a counter looking out over the lake.
features_en: Tasting counter overlooking Lake Kussharo
Operated by Teshikaga town as a designated-management project
Natural wine made from Teshikaga-grown Yamasachi grapes

yamanashi:kyoeido-winery.tagline_en: In Yamanashi's Makioka hills, Kyoeido Winery names its Koshu and Muscat Bailey A in code, dressing each vintage in artist-collaboration labels.
yamanashi:kyoeido-winery.desc_en: Kyoeido Winery was founded in 2016 in Makioka, Yamanashi City, under the philosophy of 'flourishing together,' making wine from Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) and Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red). Grapes come from the winery's own vineyards in Yamanashi and Koshu cities and from six contracted growers around the prefecture. Its wines are named with distinctive sequences of symbols and numbers rather than conventional names, and each vintage features a label created in collaboration with an artist, reflecting the winery's aim of fusing wine and art.
features_en: Founded in 2016, known for naming wines with symbol-and-number sequences instead of conventional names
Artist-collaboration labels created for every vintage
Grapes from the winery's own vineyards in Makioka plus six contracted growers across Yamanashi

fukuoka:watarise-farm-winery.tagline_en: A farming family in business since the Edo era, Fujita used a 2016 special wine-zone framework to open Kitakyushu's very first winery in 2018.
fukuoka:watarise-farm-winery.desc_en: Watarise Farm & Winery is run by Keizo Fujita, whose family has farmed in Arike, Wakamatsu Ward, Kitakyushu, since the Edo period. Using a special wine-production zone approved in October 2016, Fujita obtained a brewing license on February 26, 2018, opening Kitakyushu's first winery. The small, family-run operation grows all of its own grapes and handles every step of production in-house, working with Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Kerner, Campbell Early and Kyoho.
features_en: Family has farmed in Arike, Wakamatsu Ward, Kitakyushu since the Edo period
Used a special wine-zone framework (approved October 2016) to obtain a brewing license in February 2018, becoming Kitakyushu's first winery
100% self-grown, self-brewed winemaking

yamanashi:domaine-kayagatake.tagline_en: At the southern foot of Mt. Kayagatake, a husband-and-wife team turned a debut 2015 vintage into an award-winning small Nirasaki winery.
yamanashi:domaine-kayagatake.desc_en: Domaine Kayagatake sits at the southern foot of Mt. Kayagatake in Nirasaki. Its owner, Masahiko Abe, left a corporate career, earned an associate-level wine-chemistry qualification at the University of Yamanashi, and released his first vintage in 2015; the winery relocated to its current site in 2017. That debut vintage was selected as the best Japanese wine at the 'Nihon de Nomou: Saiko no Wine' tasting competition. The estate grows Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red) and Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) on its own vineyard, also using Merlot grown in nearby Hosaka.
features_en: Muscat Bailey A and Koshu grown on the estate's own vineyard, plus Merlot from nearby Hosaka
Winning competition awards since its debut 2015 vintage
Cultivation and winemaking run together by a husband-and-wife team

アダージョ ディ 上ノ山 マスカットベーリーA.name_en: Adagio di Uenoyama Muscat Bailey A
アダージョ ディ 上ノ山 マスカットベーリーA.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A, fruit aromatics roughly 10x typical furaneol levels, deep purple

アダージョ ディ 上ノ山 甲州.specs_en: White, dry — fully ripened, estate-grown Koshu

hyogo:kobe-winery.tagline_en: Kobe's long-running municipal winery reopened in 2025 as Kobe Agri Park, still pouring Kobe-grown wine inside a sprawling agricultural theme park.
hyogo:kobe-winery.desc_en: Kobe Winery has long been a fixture of Nishi Ward's agricultural park, and on April 12, 2025 it reopened under private management as Kobe Agri Park. Wine production and sales continue under Hakutsuru Sake Brewing Co., which took over the Kobe Wine business, using only grapes grown within Kobe, including Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Riesling. First vinified in 1983, the wine is sold and tasted on-site at a park that also houses a barbecue area, pitch-and-putt golf and go-karts, with free admission and parking.
features_en: First vintage produced in 1983
Uses only grapes grown within Kobe
Large agricultural park with a wine shop plus BBQ, putting-golf and go-kart facilities

nagano:closdetenryu-chateau-kiribayashi.tagline_en: In Iida's Kiribayashi hills, Clos de Tenryu opened in 2022 with four licenses at once, debuting an orange wine of 100% Nagano Koshu.
nagano:closdetenryu-chateau-kiribayashi.desc_en: Clos de Tenryu Chateau Kiribayashi opened in March 2022 in Kiribayashi, Iida, after simultaneously obtaining a wine brewing license, a brandy distillation license, a liqueur manufacturing license and a liquor sales license. Its debut wine, Asayake, is an orange wine made from 100% Nagano-grown Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape). The estate also grows Pinot Noir, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Viognier. Visits require an advance phone call.
features_en: Obtained wine, brandy-distillation, liqueur-manufacturing and liquor-sales licenses simultaneously in March 2022
Grows Pinot Noir, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Viognier alongside Koshu
Visits require an advance phone call

yamanashi:grandvert-vineyard.tagline_en: Grand-opened in September 2024 at 950m on Yatsugatake's slopes, Grand Vert pours Chardonnay, Koshu and Riesling with Fuji in view.
yamanashi:grandvert-vineyard.desc_en: Yatsugatake Grand Vert Vineyard held its grand opening in September 2024 on a roughly 15-hectare site at about 950 meters on the slopes of Yatsugatake in Kobuchizawa, Hokuto, growing Chardonnay, Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), Riesling and other varieties. A winery, shop and observation deck sit at the center of the vineyard, where visitors can taste wine against a backdrop of Yatsugatake and Mt. Fuji.
features_en: High-altitude, roughly 950-meter vineyard with views of Yatsugatake and Mt. Fuji
Roughly 15 hectares of vines with an on-site winery and observation deck
Grand-opened in 2024 as one of Yamanashi's newest wineries

yamanashi:rakuen-winery.tagline_en: Since 1940, this Ichikawamisato family has poured small-batch Koshu and Muscat Bailey A under its 'Albatross' label from a tiny hillside vineyard.
yamanashi:rakuen-winery.desc_en: Rakuen Vineyard was founded in 1940 in Ichikawamisato, and remains the town's only family-run winery. Grapes come from roughly 1,200 tsubo (about 0.4 hectares) of the family's own vineyard plus fruit from neighboring farms, vinified in small batches for a natural style. Its flagship label, Albatross, is known for the rich, mellow character that comes from careful small-lot production.
features_en: Founded in 1940, the only family-run winery in Ichikawamisato
Roughly 1,200 tsubo (about 0.4 hectares) of the family's own vineyard plus grapes from neighboring farms
Flagship 'Albatross' label known for rich flavor from careful small-batch production

yamanashi:la-pensee-winery.tagline_en: A new natural winery in Minami-Alps, LA PENSÉE ferments organic Koshu and Muscat Bailey A with wild yeast, naming each cuvée by numbers.
yamanashi:la-pensee-winery.desc_en: LA PENSÉE received its brewing license in September 2024, becoming a new natural winery in Minami-Alps City. Its founder, 髙橋厚芝, trained for three years at Domaine Hide as part of a local revitalization program before starting the winery. Grapes — Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), Muscat Bailey A (a Japanese-bred red) and Gewürztraminer — are organically grown, and the wines are fermented with wild yeast and made without added sulfites. Each cuvée is named with a number rather than a conventional label.
features_en: Opened in September 2024 as a new natural winery in Minami-Alps City
Wild-yeast fermentation, no added sulfites, and organically grown grapes
Cuvées named by number rather than conventional labels

420 QUATRE-DEUX-ZÉRO.specs_en: Rosé — Koshu and Muscat Bailey A blend, wild yeast, no added sulfites

524 CINQ-DEUX-QUATRE.specs_en: Sparkling rosé — Koshu, Muscat Bailey A and Gewürztraminer field blend, wild yeast, no added sulfites

yamanashi:shion-winery.tagline_en: Born from a Yokohama kindergarten's nature-education program, Shion Winery makes dry, food-friendly wines from Makioka Kyoho under flower-illustrated labels.
yamanashi:shion-winery.desc_en: Shion Winery began in 2007 as a nature-education facility for a Yokohama kindergarten, using Kyoho grapes grown in Makioka, Yamanashi City. The winery's aim is to bring family time and color to the dinner table, and it favors dry wines chosen for how well they pair with food. Its labels, illustrated with flowers, have made the wines popular as gifts.
features_en: Originated as a nature-education facility for a Yokohama kindergarten
Flower-illustrated labels popular as gifts
Built around Kyoho grapes grown in Makioka

chiba:vanvan-vineyard.tagline_en: Growing wine grapes on Yachimata's breezy plateau since 2010, this family farm opened Sawa Wines in 2021 as the town's first winery.
chiba:vanvan-vineyard.desc_en: Sawa Wines traces to a vineyard that has grown wine grapes — including Muscat Bailey A, Chardonnay and Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) — on a breezy plateau in Yachimata since 2010. Contract winemaking began in 2014, and in October 2021 the operation opened Sawa Wines, Yachimata's first winery. Its wines have circulated through limited distribution via the retailer Imadeya.
features_en: Growing wine grapes in Yachimata since 2010
Wines known through limited distribution via retailer Imadeya
Opened Sawa Wines in October 2021 as Yachimata's first winery

hokkaido:domaine-takahiko.tagline_en: In Yoichi, Domaine Takahiko farms 13 Pinot Noir clones biodynamically, fermenting whole clusters with wild yeast and little to no added sulfites.
hokkaido:domaine-takahiko.desc_en: Domaine Takahiko is run by a grower devoted to making wine in Yoichi, tending roughly 9,000 Pinot Noir vines organically in a winery converted from salvaged building materials. Thirteen clones are farmed biodynamically, and the wines are made through whole-cluster, wild-yeast fermentation with no added sulfites to only very small amounts. The winery and vineyard are not open for tours, though the observation deck can be visited freely.
features_en: Whole-cluster fermentation
Wild yeast
Biodynamic farming
No added sulfites to only minimal amounts

akita:winery-konohana.tagline_en: In Kazuno, Akita's shortest-daylight town, Winery Konohana turns wild-grape hybrids like Shokoshi into small-batch wines with a gentle, firm character.
akita:winery-konohana.desc_en: Winery Konohana makes wine from Yamabudou (wild grape) hybrid varieties in Kazuno, Akita, producing roughly 10,000 bottles a year in an almost entirely handmade operation. Akita has the shortest sunshine hours of any prefecture in Japan, and the winery describes its wines as carrying a gentle character with a firm core that comes from that climate. Grapes include Shokoshi, Wine Grand and Yama Sauvignon, fermented in stainless steel tanks.
features_en: Specializes in Yamabudou (wild grape) hybrid varieties
Almost entirely handmade, small-batch production of about 10,000 bottles a year
Stainless steel tank fermentation

hokkaido:north-creek-farm.tagline_en: Along the Yoichi River in Niki, husband and wife Masamitsu and Ayako Suzuki farm organically for wine that evokes Hokkaido's land itself.
hokkaido:north-creek-farm.desc_en: North Creek Farm was started in April 2020 by Masamitsu and Ayako Suzuki, who began growing wine grapes along the Yoichi River in Niki. The couple farms roughly 2.3 hectares and about 4,000 vines — Pinot Noir, Gewürztraminer, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Pinot Gris, Kerner and Chardonnay — organically, without herbicides, and ferments with wild yeast in pursuit of 'wine that brings Hokkaido's land to mind.' The winery obtained its brewing license in August 2024.
features_en: Small estate run by husband-and-wife team Masamitsu and Ayako Suzuki
Wild-yeast fermentation and herbicide-free organic farming
Flat vineyard land along the Yoichi River in Niki

iwate:art-paysan-winery.tagline_en: Run by a social welfare organization on a hill above Hanamaki's terraced rice fields, Art Paysan became the city's first craft wine and cider producer in 2019.
iwate:art-paysan-winery.desc_en: Art Paysan Winery sits on a hill overlooking terraced rice fields and mountains in Hanamaki, Iwate, operated by the social welfare corporation Yuwakai as part of its disability employment support work. It opened in 2019 as the first winery under Hanamaki's craft wine and cider special zone, using low-pesticide fruit — Chardonnay and apples — grown on its own farm to make wine and cider that capture the local terroir.
features_en: Operated by a social welfare corporation as disability employment support
Hanamaki craft wine and cider special zone's first winery (2019)
Set on a hill overlooking terraced rice fields
Produces both wine and cider

yamanashi:akeno-venus.tagline_en: With over 2,600 annual sunshine hours, Akeno drew a retiree turned winemaker to found this small Hokuto estate centered on Cabernet Sauvignon.
yamanashi:akeno-venus.desc_en: Domaine de la Akeno Venus was founded in 2018 in Akeno, Hokuto — a site with more than 2,600 hours of sunshine a year, among the highest in Japan. Its founder took up winemaking after retirement, studying at the Yamanashi Prefectural Agriculture and Forestry College and training at wineries around the prefecture before opening. Grapes, including Cabernet Sauvignon and Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape), are grown on the estate's own vineyard with reduced pesticide use.
features_en: Over 2,600 annual sunshine hours, among the best sites in Japan for grape-growing
Founded by a winemaker who took up the craft after retirement
Reduced-pesticide grapes grown entirely on the estate's own vineyard

アケノ ヴェニュス カベルネ・ソーヴィニョン.specs_en: Red — Cabernet Sauvignon, reduced-pesticide estate fruit

yamanashi:shigei-jozo.tagline_en: Trained at Domaine Oyamada, Jun Harada founded this natural winery in 2022, farming 2.4 hectares across Akeno, Hosaka and Ichinomiya without chemicals.
yamanashi:shigei-jozo.desc_en: Shigei Jozo was founded in 2022 by Jun Harada, who trained at Domaine Oyamada. The winery farms about 2.4 hectares of its own vineyards across Akeno, Hosaka and Ichinomiya, growing mainly European wine grape varieties without chemical pesticides or fertilizers, and ferments with wild yeast and no added sulfites. Its wines reach roughly 80 retailers nationwide, and the winery also takes on contract brewing for others.
features_en: No chemical pesticides or fertilizers; wild-yeast fermentation with no added sulfites
About 2.4 hectares of own vineyards across Akeno, Hosaka and Ichinomiya, mainly European varieties
Sold through roughly 80 retailers nationwide; also takes on contract brewing

翠翠 スズ・ブラン.specs_en: White — Koshu-led blend with small amounts of Delaware and Chardonnay

翠翠 スズ・ルージュ.specs_en: Red — Muscat Bailey A-led blend of several varieties

yamanashi:sadoya.tagline_en: Founded in 1917 in Kofu — the birthplace of Japanese wine — Sadoya still ages Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot in a 700-tsubo underground cellar.
yamanashi:sadoya.desc_en: Sadoya Winery was founded in 1917 in Kofu, a city known as the birthplace of Japanese wine in the early Meiji era. The winery began growing grapes in the Zenkoji area in 1936 and built its business on French winemaking methods, guided by a founding philosophy of a rich table where wine is enjoyed alongside food. Grapes include Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay. Visitors can tour the roughly 700-tsubo underground cellar, with its barrel-aging room, storage for traditional 1.8-liter bottles, exhibits and tasting counter, a five-minute walk from Kofu Station's north exit.
features_en: Founded in 1917 in Kofu, the birthplace of Japanese wine
Five-minute walk from Kofu Station's north exit
Roughly 700-tsubo underground cellar open for tours
Own vineyard in Kofu's Zenkoji area

yamanashi:higashi-shin-yoshu.tagline_en: Founded in 1963 by Nikkawa High classmates hoping to drink wine from grapes they grew, still made additive-free with wild yeast.
yamanashi:higashi-shin-yoshu.desc_en: Higashi Shin Yoshu was founded in 1963 by a group of Hikawa High School alumni who wanted to grow their own grapes, make wine and drink it together. The small winery practices natural winemaking — no added sulfites, unfiltered, wild-yeast fermentation — using an old-fashioned method that skips cold stabilization, so bottles are filled with their tartrate crystals intact. It releases more than 20 different labels each year from Koshu, Muscat Bailey A and Kerner, without seeking vintage-to-vintage consistency, giving each wine its own character.
features_en: No added sulfites, unfiltered, wild-yeast natural winemaking
Old-fashioned method that skips cold stabilization, bottling with tartrate crystals intact
Releases more than 20 distinct labels each year, without seeking vintage-to-vintage consistency

甲州街道栗原宿産マスカットベーリーA.name_en: Koshu Kaido Kurihara-juku Muscat Bailey A

hokkaido:kamisato-vineyard.tagline_en: Settling in Rankoshi in 2017, Kamisato Vineyard applies New Zealand-honed techniques to a 3-hectare south-facing slope, farmed herbicide-free with reduced pesticides.
hokkaido:kamisato-vineyard.desc_en: Kamisato Vineyard was established in Rankoshi in 2017, with planting beginning the following year on a south-facing, roughly 3-hectare slope. Its grower draws on viticultural experience gained in New Zealand, farming without herbicides and with reduced pesticide use — insecticide applied only twice a year — with an emphasis on grape quality and vine health. Grapes include Gewürztraminer, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc and Pinot Meunier; the winery obtained its brewing license in August 2024.
features_en: Viticulture informed by experience gained in New Zealand
Roughly 3 hectares on a south-facing slope
Herbicide-free farming with reduced pesticide use, prioritizing grape quality and vine health

iwate:shiwa-fruitspark.tagline_en: Shiwa's grape farmers are shareholders in this 2005 winery, which vinifies only Shiwa-grown fruit under a 'grown here, brewed here' philosophy.
iwate:shiwa-fruitspark.desc_en: Shiwa Fruits Park Winery was established in 2005 under a 'jien-jijō' philosophy — quality grapes grown locally ('jien') and vinified at the town's own winery ('jijō') — using only grapes grown in Shiwa to express the character of the local land. The growers who supply the fruit are also shareholders in the winery. It sits near the Michi-no-Eki Shiwa roadside station, with free tours and tastings that accommodate large tour buses.
features_en: 'Jien-jijō' (grown here, brewed here) winemaking style
Grape-growing farmers participate as shareholders
Established in 2005
Located near the Michi-no-Eki Shiwa roadside station

shimane:iwami-winery.tagline_en: At the foot of Mt. Sanbe, Iwami Winery pours Merlot, Marselan and Chardonnay amid grassland, with a starlit outdoor restaurant next door.
shimane:iwami-winery.desc_en: Iwami Winery Co. was established in October 2015 and built its brewing facility at the foot of Mt. Sanbe in Oda, beginning operations in April 2018. It is run by a group company of Hiroshima-based Sanyo Kucho Kogyo, and its site — surrounded by the grasslands of Mt. Sanbe — offers wine tasting alongside food. Grapes include Merlot, Marselan, Chardonnay, Moscato and Hokuten no Shizuku.
features_en: Wine tasting amid the grasslands surrounding Mt. Sanbe
Outdoor food court, the 'Iwami Starry Sky Restaurant,' on site
Operated by a group company of Hiroshima's Sanyo Kucho Kogyo

hokkaido:kurisawa-wines.tagline_en: In Sorachi's Kurisawa district, this family opened its vineyard in 2007 and now ferments Pinot Gris and other grapes in Georgian qvevri jars.
hokkaido:kurisawa-wines.desc_en: Kurisawa Wines is a family-run vineyard growing wine grapes in a small town in Hokkaido's Sorachi subprefecture. The family first planted its vineyard in 2007 and, in 2017, established a winery jointly with Nakazawa Vineyard. It works with qvevri, the traditional unglazed clay vessels used in Georgian winemaking, to vinify grapes including Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Auxerrois and Pinot Gris.
features_en: Vinifies in qvevri, the traditional clay vessels of Georgian winemaking
Family-run small winery
Practices horse-powered farm work

fukushima:ouse-winery.tagline_en: Halfway between Koriyama and Lake Inawashiro, this 2015 winery partners with local farmers to draw out the character of Fukushima's grapes, peaches and apples.
fukushima:ouse-winery.desc_en: Fukushima Ouse Winery was established in 2015 in the Ouse area of Koriyama, working with local farmers on both grape growing and winemaking while also exploring Fukushima's peaches, pears and apples for fruit wine. Its aim is to bring out the best of each ingredient, and it sits in a nature-filled valley roughly midway between Koriyama Station and Lake Inawashiro. Its main line, Vin de Ollage, is made entirely from Koriyama-grown grapes, including Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Black Queen.
features_en: Located in Koriyama's Ouse area
Established in 2015
Also produces fruit wine from Fukushima's peaches, pears and apples

Vin de Ollage.specs_en: Red and white — main series, 100% Koriyama-grown grapes

miyagi:ryomi-winery.tagline_en: Below Nanatsumori's peaks, Ryomi Vineyard & Winery picks 100% estate-grown grapes at peak ripeness, earning both Sakura Award and Decanter recognition.
miyagi:ryomi-winery.desc_en: Ryomi Vineyard & Winery grows 100% of its grapes — Merlot, Chardonnay and Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) — on its own vineyard at the foot of the Nanatsumori hills in Taiwa, Miyagi. Fruit is picked at peak ripeness and vinified with years of experience and technique. The winery has won recognition including the Sakura Award and from Decanter.
features_en: 100% estate-grown grapes
Located at the foot of the Nanatsumori hills
Award history including the Sakura Award and Decanter

yamanashi:beau-paysage.tagline_en: Guided by the belief that wine is born in the vineyard, Eiji Okamoto farms and vinifies almost single-handedly, crafting a hard-to-find 'phantom' wine.
yamanashi:beau-paysage.desc_en: Beau Paysage was founded in 2008 in Takane, Hokuto, under the philosophy that 'wine is not made by people — it is born in the vineyard.' Using no chemical fertilizers, herbicides or pesticides, winemaker Eiji Okamoto handles nearly every step — from growing Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Koshu (Japan's indigenous white grape) through vinification and bottling — almost entirely alone. The resulting wines are so limited that they are known at home and abroad as a hard-to-find, 'phantom' label.
features_en: Winemaker Eiji Okamoto handles nearly every step of production alone, in extremely limited quantities
Chemical-free, natural farming that puts vineyard work first
Known at home and abroad as a hard-to-find 'phantom' wine

yamanashi:seven-cedars-winery.tagline_en: Named for seven ancient cedars at Kawaguchi Asama Shrine, this Fuji-Kawaguchiko debut winery labels every bottle with its grower's name and variety.
yamanashi:seven-cedars-winery.desc_en: Seven Cedars Winery takes its name from seven large cedar trees at Kawaguchi Asama Shrine, and began brewing in August 2022 as Fuji-Kawaguchiko's first winery. Built on a philosophy of honoring the growers who tend its grapes, every label states the grower's name and variety. The winery farms four of its own plots — 御印, 霊嶽, 神免 and 二柱 — without herbicides or chemical fertilizers, growing Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Petit Manseng, Kerner, Pinot Noir and Merlot.
features_en: Fuji-Kawaguchiko's first winery, brewing since August 2022
Every label states the grower's name and grape variety, honoring those who tend the fruit
Four company-owned plots farmed without herbicides or chemical fertilizers

yamanashi:belle-foret-winery.tagline_en: Opened in 1985 as Snow Brand Belle Foret and renamed in 2002, this two-site winery pairs barrel-fermented Koshu with award-winning results.
yamanashi:belle-foret-winery.desc_en: Chateraise Belle Foret Winery opened in 1985 as Snow Brand Belle Foret, taking its current name in 2002 under Chateraise Co. It operates alongside its sister site, Katsunuma Winery, on a location looking out toward the Southern Alps and Yatsugatake. Its Koshu, barrel-fermented at Katsunuma, has won awards at the Japan Wine Competition. Grapes also include Chenin Blanc, Riesling and Schönburger, the last grown on the company's own Hokuto farm for a sweet wine.

Two-site operation alongside Katsunuma Winery
